channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Health Ministry Accused of Disrupting Cancer Drug Supplies
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Health Ministry is accused of disrupting the supply of essential cancer drugs. A parliamentary committee heard that patients are forced to pay for their own medication. The Deputy Health Minister acknowledged delays in drug deliveries, attributing them partly to the ministry's slow approval of procurement lists.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Extends Arrests for Five Individuals in GKN B Corruption Case
item.description: A Bishkek court has extended the pre-trial detention for five individuals implicated in a corruption case involving Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKN B). Among those detained are former high-ranking officials who served under former GKN B head Kamchybek Tashiev. The investigation is being handled by the Military Prosecutor's Office.

item.title: Iran Confirms Qatari Mediators' Visit to Tehran for Talks
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson confirmed a visit by Qatari mediators to Tehran, stating it's part of ongoing discussions regarding bilateral relations and Qatar's role in regional mediation. The visit aims to convey messages and present proposals amidst regional tensions. This follows reports of Qatari mediators traveling to Tehran to discuss ending the conflict with the US.

item.title: Central Asia Faces $3.59 Billion in Potential Landslide Losses, EDB Reports
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) estimates potential landslide losses in Central Asia at $3.59 billion, with road infrastructure accounting for $3.02 billion. A new brief highlights the hidden threat of landslides to critical infrastructure in regional cities and urges consideration of these risks in urban planning and development.

item.title: Serbia's Vučić Admits Defeat to Student-Led Protest Movement in Elections
item.description: Former President Aleksandar Vučić has acknowledged defeat in Serbia's parliamentary elections to a student-led protest movement. The "Students' List" is projected to win 135-140 seats, while Vučić's party is expected to secure 105. Observers compare this outcome to Viktor Orbán's recent electoral loss, potentially signaling a shift in Serbia's foreign policy towards Europe.

item.title: Three Arrested in Jordan in Connection with Deadly Church Attack
item.description: Three individuals have been arrested in Jordan suspected of carrying out an armed attack on a church in Karak province on October 23, which resulted in nine deaths and 25 injuries. The suspects were apprehended after a shootout with security forces in a deserted house. Large quantities of weapons and ammunition were seized.

item.title: Kazakhstan's New City to Feature Unique Iconic Complex with $1 Billion Investment
item.description: Construction has begun on the multifunctional Iconic Complex in Kazakhstan's new city, Gate District. Developed by US firm SOM and built by China's CSCEC, the project is expected to cost around $1 billion. The complex will house offices, apartments, a hotel, and retail spaces, serving as the heart of the business center.

item.title: EAEU Increases Tariffs on Certain Goods from Third Countries to Aid Kyrgyz Textile Industry
item.description: The Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) will raise customs duties on specific clothing and other goods imported from non-EAEU countries. This decision aims to strengthen the position of Kyrgyz textile manufacturers by making imported products more expensive, according to the Eurasian Economic Commission.

item.title: Serbian President Vučić Admits Election Defeat, Signaling Political Shift
item.description: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić has conceded defeat in parliamentary elections to a student-led protest movement. This outcome could usher in a new era in Serbian politics, potentially leading to closer ties with Europe and a distancing from Russia. Preliminary results indicate the opposition will secure a majority in parliament.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kaztsink to Earn Over $4 Billion from Gold Mine Development
item.description: Kaztsink, a subsidiary of the international trader Glencore, projects revenues exceeding $4.4 billion from the underground development of the Vasilkovskoye gold deposit in Kazakhstan. The project, located near Kokshetau, is expected to yield 40.5 tons of gold over 17 years, with operations commencing in 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan Adopts New Migration Law: What Changes for Migrant Workers?
item.description: Tajikistan's parliament has adopted a new law on migration, replacing the current law from 1999, which is considered outdated. The article promises details on how this new legislation will affect Tajik migrant workers, indicating significant changes are expected due to the updated standards.

item.title: Tajikistan and Chinese Company Sign Education Cooperation Memorandum
item.description: Tajikistan's Center for International Programs and China's Beijing Yude International Education Technology Group have signed a memorandum of understanding. The agreement aims to foster long-term educational cooperation, expand institutional ties, and enhance academic exchange between the two countries. It facilitates Tajik students pursuing higher education in China.

item.title: Taliban Announce 24-Hour Transit Operations Between Afghanistan and Iran
item.description: Transit traffic between Afghanistan's Nimroz province and Iran's Milak border crossing is now operating 24 hours a day, the Taliban announced. The head of the Taliban governor's office in Nimroz stated that daily vehicle crossings have doubled to 800 since the extended hours began. The Milak crossing is a vital trade route for both countries.

item.title: Kazakh President Congratulates Lula da Silva on Election Victory
item.description: Kazakhstan's Head of State, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, congratulated Brazil's President Lula da Silva on his election victory. Tokayev shared his congratulatory message on social media, stating that the Brazilian people support da Silva's policies aimed at strengthening national sovereignty, enhancing Brazil's global standing, reforming the UN, and establishing a just world order.

item.title: Central Asian Countries Discuss Development of Family Medicine and Nursing
item.description: A conference in Dushanbe on October 20, 2026, focused on training specialists in family medicine and nursing across Central Asia. Participants reviewed practical training experiences, discussed improving primary healthcare quality, and addressed regional needs for medical personnel. The World Health Organization's collaboration in strengthening healthcare systems was also highlighted.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Data on Wildberries Seller Losses, Awaiting Compensation
item.description: Kazakhstan is still updating data on Kazakh entrepreneurs affected by attacks on Russian Wildberries warehouses, with losses estimated at 1.45 billion tenge for over 223 sellers. The National Chamber of Entrepreneurs "Atameken" is verifying information as official compensation details from Wildberries have not been provided. The Ministry of Trade is interacting with the marketplace regarding damage assessment.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Fund Election Campaigning for Maslikhat Candidates
item.description: The Kazakh government will allocate funds to support the election campaigning of candidates running for maslikhats (local representative bodies). The specific amount to be allocated has not yet been disclosed, but it signifies state support for the electoral process at the local level.

item.title: Russian Interior Ministry Reports 40% Drop in Migrant Crime Amid Increased Checks
item.description: The Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs reports a 40% decrease in crime among migrants. Despite this reduction, the number of checks increased by 155,000, leading to a 43% rise in the number of individuals inspected. Further details are pending.

item.title: Journalist Daniyar Adilbekov Released on Probation in Kazakhstan
item.description: Journalist Daniyar Adilbekov has been released on probation in Kazakhstan, with his sentence reduced. He was initially sentenced to 4 years and 6 months for spreading false information. Human rights advocates consider his release a small victory, noting that cases involving journalists in Kazakhstan do not always end well. Adilbekov is expected to return to his profession after his probation period.

item.title: New Deputy Minister Appointed for Digitalization and Cybersecurity in Uzbekistan's Emergency Situations Ministry
item.description: Oktam Khamdamov Rustamovich has been appointed Deputy Minister for Digitalization and Cybersecurity in Uzbekistan's Ministry of Emergency Situations, according to a presidential decree. Previously, Khamdamov served as head of a department at the State Institution "Cybersecurity Center."

item.title: Tajikistan's Energy Minister Visits Site for Proposed Khutalon Hydropower Plant
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources, Daler Juma, visited the proposed construction site for the Khutalon (Shurob) Hydropower Plant on October 23, 2026. The new plant, planned on the Vakhsh River, will have a projected capacity of 800 MW and is expected to generate over 2.5 billion kWh annually.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets Campaign Spending Limits for Local Council Candidates
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has set spending limits for candidates running for local council seats. The limits vary based on the level of the council (regional, city, or district) and cover expenses for media, public events, campaign materials, and transportation. Candidate nomination closes October 27.

item.title: Uzbekistan Uncovers 471 Illegal LPG "Bunkers" Since Start of 2025
item.description: Uzbekistan's 'Hududgazta'minot' has identified 1,217 violations in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) supply since the beginning of 2025. Authorities have uncovered 471 illegal "bunkers" selling LPG and seized over 193 tons of the gas, preventing its illicit sale. Criminal cases have been initiated based on the findings.

item.title: Kazakhstan launches $1.8 billion copper smelting plant construction in Aktogay
item.description: KAZ Minerals has begun construction of a $1.8 billion copper smelting plant in Aktogay, Kazakhstan, following the approval of a new copper processing methodology. The plant is expected to produce 300,000 tons of cathode copper annually, with first production anticipated in 2030.

item.title: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi oil facilities and Riyadh airport amid escalating conflict
item.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed responsibility for attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations and Riyadh airport. The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a missile fired towards Riyadh. These actions intensify hostilities and raise concerns over oil supply disruptions.

item.title: Tashkent City Administration Promises Not to Delay Heating Season Start
item.description: The Tashkent city administration acknowledged public concerns about the start of the centralized heating season. While adhering to the regulation requiring five consecutive days below 8°C, officials stated they will consider current weather conditions and will not delay the decision if colder weather necessitates it. Preparations are underway.

item.title: 51 Children in Fergana Kindergartens Reportedly Suffered Food Poisoning
item.description: Symptoms of food poisoning have been observed among 51 children from three kindergartens in Fergana city. Affected children were hospitalized with fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Initial investigations identified food products and suppliers. Bacteriological samples have been collected for laboratory testing. The condition of the hospitalized children is stable.

item.title: Afghanistan's Central Bank to Fully Lift Bank Account Withdrawal Restrictions by Year-End
item.description: Afghanistan's Central Bank announced plans to completely remove all restrictions on bank account withdrawals for citizens by the end of the current solar year. The bank noted an increase in citizen deposits, with a growth of five billion Afghanis this year. Plans also include expanding banking services nationwide and distributing licenses for Islamic banking to six commercial banks.

item.title: Serbia's Former President Vučić Admits Defeat in Snap Parliamentary Elections
item.description: Former Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić has conceded defeat in the snap parliamentary elections held on October 25. His "Serbia Must Not Stop" party lost to the "Students' List" opposition movement. Vučić stated that the opposition is projected to win between 135 and 140 seats in the 250-seat parliament, while his party secured approximately 105 seats.

item.title: Uzbekistan Protests Iran's Diplomatic Missions Over Samarkand Heritage Posts
item.description: Uzbekistan has protested Iran's diplomatic missions for their social media posts regarding Samarkand's heritage. The Uzbek Foreign Ministry summoned Iran's ambassador and presented a protest note, stating the posts interpreted Samarkand's heritage "one-sidedly and for political purposes." Uzbekistan demanded the removal of disputed posts and measures to prevent recurrence.

item.title: Japan supports childhood vaccination in Afghanistan through UNICEF
item.description: UNICEF is providing vaccines and essential health services to children across Afghanistan with support from Japan. This partnership aims to improve children's access to healthcare and prevent polio. UNICEF expressed gratitude for Japan's long-standing cooperation, emphasizing that every child deserves a future free from polio.

item.title: CSTO to send military equipment to Tajikistan to strengthen Afghan border
item.description: The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) is set to deliver military equipment and weapons to Dushanbe this autumn. The move aims to reinforce Tajikistan's border with Afghanistan. The organization is providing necessary supplies to bolster border security in the region.

item.title: Turkmenistan: Women Resort to Illegal Abortions Due to Strict Restrictions
item.description: Women in Turkmenistan are increasingly resorting to illegal abortions due to strict legal limitations on the procedure. Since the permitted abortion window was reduced from 12 to five weeks in 2022, clandestine procedures have become more common, posing significant health risks. These illegal abortions, performed at home or in hospitals without official records, can cost between 5,000 and 20,000 manats.

item.title: Khatlon Region Produces Over Half of Tajikistan's Agricultural Output
item.description: Tajikistan's agricultural production reached 35.7 billion somoni, an 8.2% increase year-on-year. The Khatlon region contributed 53.3% of the total output. Significant gains were reported in crop yields, including grains, potatoes, vegetables, and fruits, alongside livestock production.

item.title: Kazakhstan Increases Export Prices for Various Goods
item.description: Kazakhstan has seen an average 9% increase in the price of exported goods in January-August 2026 compared to the same period last year, according to the Bureau of National Statistics. Prices rose by 3% for CIS countries and 10% for other destinations. Significant price hikes were observed in rubber, copper, and ore products.

item.title: UN-Habitat: 100 Families in Herat Gain Access to Safe Drinking Water
item.description: UN-Habitat announced that 100 families in Herat's Zinda Jan district now have access to safe drinking water, thanks to support from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). The water is connected directly to homes and available 24/7, improving health and living conditions.

item.title: Stronger Afghani Fails to Offset High Food and Fuel Costs in Afghanistan, WFP Reports
item.description: Despite a stronger Afghani currency, the World Food Program reports that prices for staple foods, fuel, and agricultural inputs remain significantly higher than last year in Afghanistan. Disruptions to regional trade routes and slower imports are exacerbating these costs. Rice prices have seen substantial year-over-year increases, with Sholae rice up 32% and Palawi rice up 18%.

item.title: UN: Phase Two of Economic Recovery Begins in Five Afghan Provinces
item.description: The United Nations has announced the commencement of the second phase of economic recovery initiatives across five provinces in Afghanistan. This phase aims to further stabilize and develop the local economies, building upon the progress made in the initial stage. Specific details regarding the projects and targeted sectors were not immediately available.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Grants First Islamic Banking License to Open Bank
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has issued the first license for Islamic financial services to Open Bank JSC. The license, effective October 23, 2026, allows the bank to offer services compliant with Islamic finance principles. The Central Bank advises citizens to verify commercial banks' licenses on the official website before using their services.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Tatarstan Establish Consortium for Snow Leopard Study
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Tatarstan have signed an agreement to create a consortium focused on studying and restoring snow leopard populations. The collaboration will involve research centers in both regions, with a focus on genetic diversity, population monitoring, and breeding techniques. The initiative also aims to establish biobanks and facilitate specialist training.
